title: Sharing in a ratio
objectives: Split an amount in a given ratio by counting equal parts
Find the parts from a total, one share or a difference
Tell a ratio from a fraction of the whole

screens.prose: Ana and Ben share 15 £1 coins in the ratio 2 : 3. They deal in rounds: 2 coins to Ana, then 3 to Ben. One round is done.

state.caption: One round dealt: 2 coins to Ana, 3 to Ben

screens.question: Keep dealing until the pot is empty. How many coins does Ana end with?

hints.text: How many coins leave the pot in each round?
Each round takes 5 coins. The pot started with 15.
15 coins make 3 rounds of 5. Ana takes 2 coins in each round.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count the rounds first, then Ana's coins in each.

byKey.one-round: You counted Ana's first round only. The dealing goes on until all 15 coins are gone.
byKey.fraction: You took two thirds of 15. Ana gets 2 coins for every 3 Ben gets, so 2 of every 5 coins.
byKey.half: You split the coins evenly. Ben takes more in every round, so Ana ends with less than half.

explain.text: Each round deals 5 coins, so the 15 coins last 3 rounds. Ana gets 2 coins a round, 6 in all, and Ben gets 9. Notice that 6 : 9 still compares as 2 : 3.

screens.prose: Here is the same deal laid out as a grid. Each row is one round. Ana takes the first 2 coins of every round, Ben the next 3. Tap a coin to select it.

state.caption: Each row is one round of 5 coins

screens.question: Tap every coin Ana receives.

hints.text: Which columns belong to Ana?
Ana's columns are the first two.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Tap Ana's coins in every round, and only those.

byKey.one-round: You tapped round 1 only. Ana takes 2 coins in every round.
byKey.ben: You tapped Ben's coins. Ana's are in the first two columns.
byKey.c13: That coin is in one of Ben's columns.
byKey.c23: That coin is in one of Ben's columns.
byKey.c33: That coin is in one of Ben's columns.
byKey.c14: That coin is in one of Ben's columns.
byKey.c15: That coin is in one of Ben's columns.
byKey.c21: Ana's coin from round 2 is missing.
byKey.c31: Ana's coin from round 3 is missing.

explain.text: Ana owns 2 whole columns and Ben owns 3. Every column holds the same 3 coins. So 2 : 3 counts equal columns, and the coins, 6 : 9, compare the same way.

screens.prose: Each column you tapped is one **part**. In a ratio every part is the same size. Cara and Dev share £40 in the ratio 3 : 2, so Cara has 3 parts and Dev has 2.
screens.question: How much does Cara get?

hints.text: How many equal parts make the £40?
The bar has 3 + 2 = 5 parts.
One part is £40 ÷ 5 = £8. Cara has 3 parts.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find one part first, then take Cara's 3 parts.

byKey.one-part: £8 is one part. Cara has 3 parts.
byKey.dev: That is Dev's 2 parts. Cara has the other 3.
byKey.by-three: You divided £40 by 3. The bar has 5 parts, not 3.

explain.text: There are 3 + 2 = 5 parts, so one part is £40 ÷ 5 = £8. Cara has 3 parts, £24, and Dev has £16. Check: £24 + £16 = £40.

screens.prose: Three people now. Eve, Fin and Gus share £60 in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3.

state.caption: Eve 1 part, Fin 2 parts, Gus 3 parts

screens.question: How much does Gus get?

hints.text: Add the ratio numbers to count the parts.
Gus owns the last 3 of the 6 parts.
One part is £60 ÷ 6 = £10. Gus has 3 parts.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count all the parts, find one, then take Gus's 3.

byKey.one-part: £10 is one part. Gus has 3 of them.
byKey.by-people: You split £60 between 3 people equally. The ratio gives Gus more than the others.
byKey.by-ratio-sum: You used 5 parts, as if Eve were not there. The bar has 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 parts.

explain.text: The three numbers add to 6 parts, so one part is £10. Gus gets 3 parts, £30. Eve gets £10 and Fin £20, and the three add to £60.

screens.prose: This time we know one share, not the total. Hal and Isla share some money in the ratio 2 : 5. Hal gets £14.
screens.question: How much does Isla get?

hints.text: What is one part worth?
Hal's £14 fills 2 parts.
One part is £14 ÷ 2 = £7. Isla has 5 parts.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Use Hal's 2 parts to find one part.

byKey.add-gap: You added 3, the gap between 2 and 5. A ratio scales by parts: each of Isla's 5 parts is £7.
byKey.total: That is all 7 parts. Isla has 5 of them.
byKey.frac: You took two fifths of £14. Hal's £14 is 2 parts, so one part is £7.

explain.text: Hal's 2 parts hold £14, so one part is £7. Isla has 5 parts: 5 × £7 = £35. We never needed the total, though it is £49.

screens.prose: Now only a difference is known. Jo and Kit share money in the ratio 3 : 5. Kit gets £18 more than Jo.
screens.question: What is the total amount shared?

hints.text: How many more parts does Kit have than Jo?
Kit's extra 2 parts hold the £18.
One part is £18 ÷ 2 = £9. The bar has 8 parts.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The £18 is the value of Kit's extra parts.

byKey.diff-as-part: You treated £18 as one part. It is the gap of 5 − 3 = 2 parts, so one part is £9.
byKey.kit: That is Kit's share. The question asks for both shares together.
byKey.jo: That is Jo's share. Add Kit's £45 for the total.

explain.text: Kit has 5 − 3 = 2 more parts, and those 2 parts hold £18. So one part is £9, and all 8 parts make £72. Jo gets £27 and Kit £45, which differ by £18.

screens.prose: A fund holds bonds and shares in the ratio 2 : 3.
screens.question: What fraction of the whole fund is bonds?

options.why: You read 2 : 3 as a fraction. That compares bonds with shares only, but the whole fund is all 5 parts.

canvas.caption: 2/3 puts the shares' 3 parts on the bottom

options.why: That is the shares' fraction. Bonds are the other 2 parts.
You divided shares by bonds. That compares the two holdings and is bigger than the whole fund.

hints.text: How many parts is the whole fund?
The whole fund is every part in the bar.
Bonds fill 2 of the 2 + 3 = 5 parts.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compare the bonds with the whole fund, not with the shares.

byKey.as-fraction: You read 2 : 3 as a fraction. That compares bonds with shares, but the whole fund is 5 parts.

explain.text: Bonds are 2 parts out of 2 + 3 = 5, so they are $\tfrac{2}{5}$ of the fund. The $\tfrac{2}{3}$ compares bonds with shares, not with the whole. A ratio $a : b$ gives the fractions $\tfrac{a}{a+b}$ and $\tfrac{b}{a+b}$.

screens.prose: Each time you counted the parts, found one part, then multiplied. For a total $T$ in the ratio $a : b$: $$\text{first share} = \frac{a}{a+b} \times T, \qquad \text{second share} = \frac{b}{a+b} \times T$$
screens.question: £90 is shared in the ratio 4 : 5. Which calculation gives the second share?

options.why: You put the other share on the bottom. That compares the two shares and gives more than the £90 itself.
That is one fifth of £90. The total splits into 4 + 5 = 9 parts, not 5.
You took the ratio number away. A ratio splits the total into equal parts; it never subtracts a fixed amount.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count all the parts, then take the second person's share of them.

explain.text: There are 4 + 5 = 9 parts, so the second share is $\tfrac{5}{9} \times 90 = 50$, which is £50. The first share is £40, and £40 + £50 = £90.

screens.prose: Share £84 in the ratio 3 : 4 the way you did on the bars. Each line uses the line before it.
screens.question: Put the lines in order.

lines.text: Count the parts: $3 + 4 = 7$, adding the ratio numbers
One part: $84 \div 7 = 12$, since every part is equal
Second share: $84 - 36 = 48$, what is left of the total

hints.text: Which number must you know before you can find one part?
The number of parts comes from the ratio alone.
Parts, then one part, then the first share, then what is left, then the check.

feedback.correct: Each line needs the one before it.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Start with what the ratio alone tells you.

byKey.one: One part needs the number of parts, so counting the parts comes first.
byKey.second: The second share here is what is left after the first, so the first share comes before it.

explain.text: You counted 7 parts, found one part, £12, and took 3 of them for £36. The rest, £48, is the second share. Dividing 36 : 48 by 12 returns 3 : 4, so the split is right.

screens.prose: You hold £25,000 split 60 : 40 between shares and bonds: £15,000 and £10,000. A month later the shares are worth £16,500 and the bonds are unchanged.
screens.question: How much of the shares must you sell, and move into bonds, to get back to 60 : 40?

hints.text: Find the new total first.
The target gives shares 3 parts out of 5 of the new total.
The new total is £26,500, so one part is £5,300. Shares should hold 3 parts.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Apply 3 : 2 to the new total, then compare with the shares you hold.

byKey.sold-gain: You sold the whole £1,500 gain. Rebalancing splits the new total of £26,500, so shares keep 60% of the gain.
byKey.swapped: You gave shares 40% of the total. The split is shares to bonds, so shares get the 60%.

explain.text: The new total is £26,500, so one part of 5 is £5,300. Shares should hold 3 parts, £15,900, so you sell £600. Bonds rise to £10,600, and 15,900 : 10,600 is 3 : 2.

ideas: A ratio $a : b$ splits an amount into $a + b$ equal parts.
Find one part first, from the total, from one share or from a difference. Then multiply.
The fraction of the whole is $\dfrac{a}{a+b}$, not $\dfrac{a}{b}$.

formula.name: Sharing in a ratio
formula.note: Check that the shares add back to the total.

summary.trap: 2 : 3 does not mean two thirds of the whole. The whole has 5 parts, so the first share is two fifths.

quiz.prose: £100 is shared in the ratio 1 : 2. Amounts are paid to the nearest penny.
quiz.question: How much is the smaller share?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The total splits into 1 + 2 = 3 parts.

byKey.half: You took half of £100. The ratio 1 : 2 makes 3 parts, and the smaller share is 1 of them.
byKey.third-up: You rounded up. £33.333... rounds down to £33.33; the extra penny goes to the larger share.

explain.text: One part is £100 ÷ 3 = £33.333..., which rounds to £33.33. The larger share is then £66.67, so the two still add to £100. When the parts do not divide exactly, one penny of rounding lands on one side.

quiz.prose: A fund holds cash and shares in the ratio 1 : 4.
quiz.question: What percentage of the fund is cash?

options.why: You read 1 : 4 as one quarter. The whole fund is 1 + 4 = 5 parts.
That is the shares' percentage. Cash is the 1 part.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compare cash with the whole fund.

explain.text: The fund is 1 + 4 = 5 parts, and cash is 1 of them. One fifth is 20%. The 25% comes from treating the ratio as a fraction.

quiz.prose: Two partners split a profit in the ratio 5 : 3. The smaller share is £1,200.
quiz.question: What is the total profit?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The smaller share is 3 parts.

byKey.larger: That is the larger share. Add the £1,200 for the total.
byKey.wrong-part: You treated £1,200 as 5 parts. The smaller share is the 3 parts.
byKey.one-part: £400 is one part. The total is 8 parts.

explain.text: The smaller share is 3 parts, so one part is £1,200 ÷ 3 = £400. The total is 5 + 3 = 8 parts, £3,200. The larger share is £2,000.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Add all three ratio numbers to count the parts.

byKey.by-people: You split £1,500 between three people equally. The ratio gives the largest share 5 of 10 parts.
byKey.one-part: £150 is one part. The largest share is 5 parts.

explain.text: The parts add to 2 + 3 + 5 = 10, so one part is £150. The largest share is 5 parts, £750. The others are £300 and £450.
